facts.fact: The Regulation 19 housing chapter states a plan-period minimum of 33,280 new dwellings for 2019–2041.
Table 8.1 identifies sites proposed to be allocated for housing and, where appropriate, mixed-use development.
The proposed allocation boundaries are defined on the Enfield Policies Map.
The site-selection methodology prioritises development of brownfield sites.
Appendix C site proformas carry policy status and set site requirements and considerations.
SA1.1 is Palace Gardens Shopping Centre, proposed for mixed use, with estimated capacity 329.
SA1.2 is Enfield Town Station and the Former Enfield Arms, Genotin Road, with estimated capacity 79.
SA1.3 is Tesco Superstore, Southbury Road, with estimated capacity 303.
SA1.4 is Enfield Civic Centre, with estimated capacity 114.
SA1.5 is St Anne’s Catholic High School for Girls, proposed for housing, with estimated capacity 131.
SA1.6 is 100 Church Street, Enfield, proposed for housing, with estimated capacity 78.
SA1.7 is Oak House, 43 Baker Street, proposed for housing, with estimated capacity 47.
SA2.1 is Colosseum Retail Park, proposed for mixed use, with estimated capacity 1,587.
SA2.3 is Morrisons, Southbury Road, proposed for mixed use, with estimated capacity 646.
SA2.4 is Southbury Leisure Park, proposed for mixed use, with estimated capacity 605.
SA2.5 is Tesco store, Ponders End, 288 High Street, with estimated capacity 521.
SA2.6 is Sainsbury’s Crown Road, proposed for mixed use, with estimated capacity 868.
SA2.6 design principles require improved east–west pedestrian connections between the A10 and Baird Road.
SA2.6 should provide a green spine linking Enfield Playing Fields to the adjacent Colosseum Retail Park allocation.
A named allocation and capacity table is authoritative plan evidence but does not by itself prove parcel_30762 intersects the mapped polygon.
